reason:
FEASIBILITY: the out-of-sample core (Stage 1, dorado boxes) cannot be done in time to act on; only the CPU Stage 0 is feasible, and it is narrow.
(1) Stage 1 cost is understated. The zarr chunks are (1,1,128,2217,2170), about 400 MB each, so 24 boxes need about 40 GB. At the logged 2-10 MB/s that is 1.1-5.5 h of streaming. On top of that: a pixel-identity check, ~1 day of glue, and FULL caches for BOTH exp48 and exp51 (raw ILP, ckpt, DeepCenter pass-1 extras, DivNet) generated on friend A's GPU, whose availability is unknown. The earliest verdict is 27 Sep, which leaves 2 days and ~10 probes. The claimed '1 GPU-h' and the +-0.0005 resolution do not hold: 24 boxes come from one or two late (t >= 380) slab windows and are correlated, so the realistic resolution is about +-0.001-0.0015.
(2) Stage 0 is feasible and testable in the existing replay lab (fixed nodes and edge probabilities; methodology only, so no conflict with relink, gap closing, safe divisions, leaf prune, DaughterNet or the edge filter). Evidence: confirmation replay of 135 videos took 488 s (2-20 s per video). build_dense_gt.py already writes GT-format geffs with estimated_number_of_nodes copied. tracks.npz holds tracklet start/end/parent, so division cuts are trivial. Needed glue: init_context asserts score_geffs.DATA == data_dir, and DATA is read from the environment at import, so a separate GT-dir must be added, ideally scoring each prediction against all 6 GT sets in one pass. kaggle_lab.py drops --data-dir (DROPPED_OPTS) and needs a --gt-dir passthrough plus a small private dataset. Replay bootstraps by video, so a post-hoc 11-leak-group bootstrap is needed. Prediction geffs are deleted by default, so the configs must be re-run (cheap). Total ~1 agent-day, verdict late 25 Sep.
(3) But Stage 0 can decide little of what the hypothesis lists:
- ef_a0, ef_a3_rl_pr and the stitch bundle are already settled by probes 29/30 (the stitch bundle was closed with the edge filter), so they serve only as calibration.
- Float coords come from a separate coordinate-rewrite harness, are LB-probed on 25 Sep anyway, and pseudo-GT noise (1.29 um) matches the effect size.
- Coordhead / the exp51 multiplier question needs exp51 train caches, which do not exist (~63 videos of GPU inference + DC + DivNet).
- Fork-midpoint is a division item, and the pseudo-GT has no forks.
That leaves frozen ILP-first, overlap consensus and the edge side of fork-midpoint. Each is ~+0.001, against a Stage-0 CI of about +-0.001 with only 11 independent leak groups (overlapping crops count the same pseudo-edges several times, so the '240k edges' is not the effective sample size). A true +0.001 item passes the proposed gate about half the time.
(4) Calibration rests on 3 LB points, each +-0.002-0.003 noisy, and can only detect a large effect (+0.016 vs ~0). The seen/unseen contrast is also confounded: Ultrack's motion/overlap links may share our relink's errors, which also makes ILP-trusting changes look small on the unseen arm. The seen arm (tracklets cut at > 6 um steps, >= 80% of points within 3 um of GT) only partly tests this.
fix_if_any:
Drop Stage 1 (dorado OOS boxes, streaming, new GPU caches) entirely; it cannot finish before ~27 Sep. Keep a time-boxed Stage 0 only, killed if there is no verdict by 25 Sep 23:59 UTC:
(a) tools/pseudo_gt_dorado.py. Reuse the geff writer and metadata copy in build_dense_gt.py. Write real host N_est. Refit integer shifts. Cut at divisions and at > 6 um steps. Keep pieces >= 20 frames. Build a seen arm plus 3 (not 5) unseen 10% draws. This is ~4 h and runs < 5 min at nice 19.
(b) Replay patch: a --gt-dirs list scored in one pass per prediction, decoupled from the tail data_dir (removes the DATA == data_dir assert coupling). Add a --gt-dir passthrough in kaggle_lab.py plus a private dataset of the ~250 small geffs. Add a post-hoc bootstrap over the 11 leak groups.
(c) Configs: exp39, ef_a0 and ef_a3_rl_pr as LB-anchored calibration. Frozen ILP-first and overlap consensus as the only items to judge. Do NOT include float coords or coordhead: there are no exp51 caches and the judge is at the noise floor for coordinates.
(d) Pre-register the use: Stage 0 can only VETO an ILP-trusting bundle item (unseen-arm delta <= 0 with the calibration passing), never promote one. That is the only decision its +-0.001 resolution supports.
If the calibration fails (unseen-arm ef_a3_rl_pr >= +0.010, or a seen-arm sign mismatch on >= 1 of 3 anchors), stop; do not escalate to Stage 1.
realistic_public_gain: 0 direct. Stage 0 alone is worth about +0.000..+0.001 in expectation, as a veto that may keep one in-sample-artefact item (probe-30 type, -0.001) out of the final bundle. Stage 1 as proposed gives ~0 because its verdict would come too late (27 Sep+) to act on with the remaining probes.
